class.name: EnetHostedMeshTransport
class.brief_description: Mesh transport for [TickNetwork] between players over the internet, with a host that introduces and relays them.
class.description:
One node hosts the mesh ([method create_host]) and is player 1; it must be reachable on its port (a public address, or a port forwarded by the project). The other players join through it ([method create_player]) and get their id from it. The host introduces every pair of players: each player of the pair opens a socket, the host learns its public endpoint, and both punch through their NATs to connect directly. A pair that can't connect within [member punch_timeout] is relayed by the host. The engines see every player as connected either way; [method get_peer_path] tells how a player is reached. The sender of every packet comes from the connection, and the host assigns the ids: a player can't take another one's place. A relayed packet carries its origin, written by the host. The same mesh can carry [SceneMultiplayer] ([method get_multiplayer_peer]), so RPCs, spawners and synchronizers reach every player, relayed ones included. [codeblock] # On the host: var mesh := EnetHostedMeshTransport.create_host(9500) # On a player: var mesh := EnetHostedMeshTransport.create_player("203.0.113.7", 9500)
multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = mesh.get_multiplayer_peer() $Game.start(mesh) [/codeblock] [b]DTLS:[/b] pass [TLSOptions] to [method create_host] ([method TLSOptions.server]) and [method create_player] ([method TLSOptions.client], or [method TLSOptions.client_unsafe] for testing) to encrypt every link. The direct links between players use a certificate each player generates when it joins; the host hands it to the other player of the pair, who accepts only that certificate. A DTLS socket only takes DTLS, so the players register their endpoints on a second, plain port of the host (the rendezvous port, the next port by default), which must be reachable too; only single-use tokens go through it. [b]Note:[/b] the host doesn't migrate: if it leaves, the mesh ends.

method.name: close
method.description: Closes every connection. On the host, the mesh ends for every player.

method.name: create_host
method.description: Hosts a mesh on [param port] for up to [param max_players] players (the host included). The [param compression] mode must be the same on every node. With [param tls_options] ([method TLSOptions.server]), the mesh uses DTLS, and the pairs register on [param rendezvous_port] ([param port] + 1 when 0). Returns [code]null[/code] on failure.

method.name: create_player
method.description: Joins the mesh hosted at [param address]:[param port]; the id comes from the host (see [method get_status]). With [param tls_options] ([method TLSOptions.client] or [method TLSOptions.client_unsafe]), the host must use DTLS too; [param tls_hostname] is the name checked in the host's certificate ([param address] when empty). Joining with DTLS generates an RSA key for the player, which can take a moment. Returns [code]null[/code] on failure.

method.name: get_multiplayer_peer
method.description: Returns a [TickMultiplayerPeer] on this mesh, always the same one. Assign it to [member MultiplayerAPI.multiplayer_peer] to use RPCs next to the [TickNetwork].

method.name: get_peer_path
method.description: Returns how this node reaches [param peer].

method.name: get_peers
method.description: Returns the ids of the connected nodes.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns a [Dictionary] with [code]direct_pairs[/code] and [code]relayed_pairs[/code] (on a player, its links; on the host, the relayed pairs), [code]relayed_packets[/code] (host), [code]rejected_connections[/code] and [code]failed_punches[/code].

method.name: get_status
method.description: Returns the connection status. A player is [constant STATUS_CONNECTING] until the host gives it an id.

members.member: When [code]false[/code], this player never tries direct links: every other player is relayed by the host. Set it before joining.
